title: Sprains and strains
claims: A sprain is a torn or twisted ligament, most common in wrists, ankles, thumbs and knees; a strain is an overstretched or torn muscle.
Likely sprain or strain signs include pain, tenderness or weakness around the joint, swelling or bruising, inability to put weight on the injury or use it normally, and muscle spasms.

For the first 2 to 3 days NHS advises PRICE: Protection, Rest, Ice for up to 20 minutes every 2 to 3 hours, Compression, and Elevation; heat, alcohol and massage are avoided in the first couple of days.
When the injured area can be moved without pain stopping you, keep moving it so the joint or muscle does not become stiff.
Most sprains and strains feel better after 2 weeks; strenuous exercise such as running should be avoided for up to 8 weeks because of further damage risk, and severe cases can take months.

Get NHS 111 advice if the injury is very painful or worsening, there is large or worsening swelling or bruising, you cannot put any weight on it or walk more than a few steps, it feels very stiff or difficult to move, it has not improved after self-care, or you have a high temperature with hot, cold or shivery feelings suggesting infection.

Call 999 or go to A&E if you heard a crack at the injury, the body part has changed shape or points at an odd angle, it is numb, tingling or has pins and needles, or the skin around it is blue/grey or cold to touch.
